title: Introduce Cost Watchtower automation and reservoir cache profiles
author: Olivia Park
commits: 7 commits: scaffolding cost-watchtower controller; add reservoir cache profile schema; implement policy engine and safety-curve translator; CLI and admin APIs; helm chart and values; integration tests and simulator; docs and runbook
description:
Motivation: teams repeatedly tune batching, cache allocation and quantization per workload to hit unit-econ targets. Manual tuning is slow and error-prone. This PR introduces Cost Watchtower: an automated controller + CLI that continuously observes tenant unit economics (cost/token, p95 latency, reuse ratio) and applies conservative adjustments to batching, cache slice allocation and quantization aggressiveness using a new "reservoir cache profile" format and a safety-curve translator.

What this changes: introduces a new process (cmd/cost-watchtower) that can run as a standalone control-plane sidecar or as a cluster service behind the Redwood Console. The controller collects summarized per-tenant signals (telemetry ingestion via internal/telemetry), scores economics against per-tenant goals, and proposes or applies changes through the existing runtime policy API. Changes are always gated by safety curves and tenant-level cooldowns to avoid oscillations.

Key concepts: reservoir cache profiles: small JSON/YAML descriptors that describe how a tenant's KV/prefix cache should be partitioned and how much spare capacity to reserve for bursts. safety curve: maps observed latency/cost deltas to allowed quantization steps and batching targets (e.g., conservative -> -2 quant steps; permissive -> -4). cost smoothing: an exponential moving average window (configurable) that prevents reacting to single spike events.

Operational model: Cost Watchtower supports three modes: dry-run (no mutations, only suggested ops), manual-approve (creates an admin review task in Linear + annotated diff), and auto-apply (applies changes with canary routing to a configurable tenant percentage and automatic rollback on SLA breaches).

Backward compatibility: profiles are additive and opt-in; existing tenant configs are not modified by default. Controller will only act on tenants that have opted into the automated tier or when a tenant-specific override is present.

Testing and rollout: included integration e2e harness (tests/integration) that runs the controller against the cost-simulator workloads. We validated on a small staging fleet with three tenants for two weeks; no regressions in p99 latency and median cost dropped ~12% for the sampled workloads.

Docs & runbook: docs/ops/cost-watchtower.md contains configuration reference, troubleshooting, and rollback steps. Helm chart added under deploy/helm/cost-watchtower with sane defaults and a toggle to enable dry-run by default.

Checklist: - [x] Controller loop and policy engine implemented - [x] Reservoir profile schema and generator - [x] CLI for dry-run and apply - [x] Helm chart and default values - [x] Integration tests and simulator scenarios - [x] Docs and runbook
review_conversation: Marcus Lee (reviewer): The safety-curve mapping looks reasonable but we need clearer defaults for enterprise tenants; can we add a more conservative default and document the risk envelope?
Olivia Park (author): Added a second safety tier 'enterprise-safe' with smaller quantization steps and bumped the default cooldown to 30m. Documented risk envelope in docs/ops/cost-watchtower.md
Priya Nair (reviewer): Concern about telemetry cardinality — are we aggregating per-tenant at the right resolution to avoid high ingestion cost?

Olivia Park (author): The controller consumes aggregated rollups produced by existing sampling aggregator (internal/telemetry/metrics_costs.go) at 1m granularity. We added a config knob to lower to 5m for high-cardinality tenants. Added notes to runbook.
Jonah Becker (reviewer): Integration test flaked once on the canary rollback path; can we add deterministic backstop in the test harness?
Olivia Park (author): Added deterministic fixture and a synthetic SLA violation generator to the e2e test so rollback path is exercised reliably. CI re-ran and passed.

release_notes: Introduce Cost Watchtower: automated controller for tenant unit-economics with reservoir cache profiles and safety-curve driven quant/batch adjustments; CLI for dry-run/manual-approve/auto-apply; helm chart and runbook. Impact: can reduce per-tenant token cost under typical workloads by conservatively applying batching and quantization. Opt-in by default; enterprise-safe profile available.
